label: Busyness opinion
summary: A short linking phrase picked from three: "worse still, ", "thankfully" or "but at least".
details: The entries are named lazy, diligent and neutral, and the phrases match them in that order. The game's documentation does not say what decides which one is used, so the link to a character's attitude to work rests on those entry names. It runs on a character and is meant to sit inside a longer sentence.

label: Byzantine coin
summary: The name of a Byzantine coin, shown as a clickable glossary entry, or just the word "coin".
details: Entries cover the solidus (Solidi), the hyperpyron (Hyperpyra) and a plain "coin" fallback. The two coin names are glossary links (to the entry BYZANTINE_COINAGE_GLOSS). It runs on a province.

label: Camp party riddle answer
summary: The answer to one of the riddles in the camp party event (event 1010 of the camp party set).
details: There are eight answers. Four are documented with their text: iron, the moon, a table and a needle. It runs on a character.

label: Capital holding building
summary: The display name of a building in the character's capital holding, for temple, city, castle or temple citadel at levels 1 to 4.
details: The game's documentation lists 16 entries (4 holding types times 4 levels). Each one prints the name of the matching building, for example the temple_01 building. The game's documentation does not say what decides which entry is used. It runs on a character.

label: Capital building, level 2
summary: The name of the level 2 capital building: temple, city, castle or temple citadel.
details: One entry per holding type, each printing the name of the building with the suffix 02. It runs on a character.

label: Capital building, level 3
summary: The name of the level 3 capital building: temple, city, castle or temple citadel.
details: One entry per holding type, each printing the name of the building with the suffix 03. It runs on a character.

label: Capital building, level 4
summary: The name of the level 4 capital building: temple, city, castle or temple citadel.
details: One entry per holding type, each printing the name of the building with the suffix 04. It runs on a character.

label: Own or liege's title name
summary: The name of the character's own primary title, or of their liege's primary title.
details: One entry prints the name of the character's primary title without its tier word, the other does the same for the liege's primary title. The game's documentation does not say what decides which one is used. It runs on a character.

label: Cat or dog
summary: The word "cat" or the word "dog".
details: The entries are named love_cat and love_dog. The game's documentation does not say what decides which word is used. Vanilla uses it in plural form in an event text about a liege's subjects who adore them. It runs on a character.

label: Catholic saint
summary: The name of a Catholic saint, without the word "Saint".
details: The game's documentation lists 160 saints, such as Augustine of Hippo, Benedict of Nursia and David of Wales. The game marks this one as usable for picking a random entry. It runs on a character.

label: Ceiling or canopy
summary: The word "canopy" or the word "ceiling".
details: It runs on a character. The game's documentation does not say what decides which word is used.

label: Ceremonial liege or liege title
summary: A name for the top liege of the character: how the holder of a special administrative title is called, or how the top liege is called.
details: The first entry takes the top liege's primary title, reads the title saved in its variable administrative_ui_special_title and prints how that title's holder is named by title. The second prints the top liege's own title as a name. It runs on a character.

label: Chamber or tent
summary: The word "tent" or the word "chamber".
details: Vanilla uses it as the place of a character's private room in event texts ("my chamber", "his chamber"). The game's documentation does not say what decides tent or chamber. It runs on a character.

label: Chambers or tent
summary: The word "tent" or the plural "chambers".
details: Note the mix: the tent entry is singular, the chamber entry is plural. It runs on a character.

label: Contest status phrase
summary: A short phrase saying how the character stands in a contest: spectating, competing, not qualified, knocked out and so on.
details: The phrases shown are "are spectating the", "are competing in the", "did not qualify for the" and "got knocked out of". The game's documentation also lists entries for disqualified and resigned. The participating entry is listed twice. It runs on a character.

label: Chariot comeback description
summary: A phrase describing a charioteer who surges from the back of the pack to challenge the leaders.
details: There are eleven entries: blazing, sprinting, surging, dashing, rocketing, bursting, miracle, rallying, soaring, propelling and a fallback. Each is a clause such as "sprinting forward from the end, rapidly closing in on the leaders". It runs on a character.

label: Middle placement
summary: The ordinal word for a middle place in a chariot race: third, fourth or fifth.
details: The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry, so a text can name a random middling place. It runs on a character.

label: Chariot race placement
summary: The ordinal word for a finishing place in a chariot race, from first to twelfth.
details: There are twelve entries, from "first" to "twelfth". It runs on a character.

label: Chariot team color
summary: The color word of a chariot racing team: blue, green, white or red.
details: It runs on a character.

label: Chariot team name
summary: The plural team name of a chariot team: Venetoi (blue), Prasinoi (green), Leukoi (white) or Rhousioi (red).
details: The entry keys (chariot_team_blues and so on) and the linked glossary entries (BLUE_VENETOI_GLOSS and so on) tie each name to its color. It runs on a character.

label: Chariot team name, glossary link
summary: The same team names as the plain version (Venetoi, Prasinoi, Leukoi, Rhousioi), but as clickable glossary entries.
details: Each name opens its own glossary explanation (for example BLUE_VENETOI_GLOSS). It runs on a character.

label: Chariot team name, possessive
summary: The possessive form of a team name: Venetoi's, Prasinoi's, Leukoi's or Rhousioi's.
details: It runs on a character.

label: Chariot team possessive, link
summary: The possessive team names (Venetoi's and so on) as clickable glossary entries.
details: Each name links to the same glossary entry as the non-possessive linked version, with 's added. It runs on a character.

label: Wager target name
summary: The name of whoever a chariot race wager was placed on: a charioteer's first name, or a team name with "the" in front.
details: The first entry takes the character saved in the player's variable wager_target and prints their first name. The other four print "the" plus the team's plural name, taken from the game's existing texts chariot_team_blues, chariot_team_greens, chariot_team_whites and chariot_team_reds. It runs on a character.

label: Child or children
summary: The word "child" or the word "children".
details: One entry is singular, the other plural. It runs on a character.

label: Child education focus
summary: The name of the skill a child's education focuses on: diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue or learning.
details: Each entry points to the game's existing text for that education type (for example education_diplomacy_loc). It runs on a character.

label: Invalid reason word
summary: One of three words: "child", the display name of the Incapable trait, or "helpless".
details: The entries are named invalid_child, invalid_incapable and invalid_helpless, which suggests it names a reason a character does not qualify for something. The game's documentation does not say for what or what decides the word. It runs on a character.

label: Invalid reason word, possessive
summary: The possessive form of the three words: "child's", the Incapable trait name with 's, or "helpless'".
details: Same three cases as GetChildInvalid. The game's documentation does not say what decides which one is used. It runs on a character.

label: Chosen journey skill
summary: The skill chosen for a journey (diplomacy, learning, martial, stewardship or intrigue), shown with its icon, or the entry choose_on_arrival.
details: Vanilla uses it on a journey activity in the line "Chosen skill: ...". The game's documentation lists six entries: five skill prefixes and choose_on_arrival. The first four print a skill icon; the text of intrigue and choose_on_arrival is not documented. The game's documentation says it works in any scope.

label: Saga or chronicle
summary: The word "saga" or the word "chronicle".
details: It runs on a character. The game's documentation does not say what decides which word is used.

label: Ci poem name
summary: The title of a ci poem, such as Riverside City, Green Jade Bowl or Lady Yu.
details: The game's documentation lists 67 titles. Two appear twice in the list (rain_hits_a_bell and the_song_of_tangduo). The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry. It runs on a character.

label: Ci poem quality
summary: A sentence judging how good a ci poem is: weak, middling or great.
details: The weak one calls the poem ably put together but unoriginal. The middle one praises its craftsmanship and promise. The great one calls it deeply moving. The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry. It runs on a character.

label: Ci poem theme
summary: The theme of a ci poem, such as love, nature, longing or separation.
details: There are nine themes: love, nature, longing, separation, sadness and pain, philosophy, mythological events, daily chores and historical events. The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry. It runs on a character.

label: Civil appointment law
summary: The name of the meritocratic or the celestial appointment succession law.
details: Each entry prints the display name of that law. It runs on a character.

label: Clerical region map tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the clerical regions map mode for a province, depending on whether the region is held.
details: The four variants are: held with a divergent rite, held, unheld (no holder), and not part of any clerical region. The held ones show the region title, its holder and the region's rite. The divergent one also shows the county's own rite. It runs on a province.

label: Clothing article
summary: The word "shirt", "blouse" or "dress".
details: The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry. It runs on a character.

label: Co-ruler spouse title
summary: A title word: the title of the liege's primary spouse, or one of the fixed words Empress, Emperor, Queen, King, Duchess, Duke, Countess, Count, Baroness or Baron.
details: The first entry prints the title of the primary spouse of the character's liege, as a name. The others are fixed words for each rank and gender. The co-ruler meaning comes from the key and entry names; the game's documentation does not say what decides the entry. It runs on a character.

label: Fancy color description
summary: A flowery description of a color, such as sparkling golden saffron or dark midnight blue.
details: Vanilla uses it to describe the color of clothes and of a perfume. There are nine entries: gold, silver, blue, red, purple, pink, green, bronze and black. The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry. It runs on a character.

label: Tournament phase name
summary: The name of a tournament phase: Joust, Wrestling, Board Game or Duel.
details: It runs on a character.

label: Horse race name
summary: The name of a horse race, built from one or two parts.
details: One entry prints the first name part only. The other prints the first part followed by a second part. Both parts come from two other custom texts, ContestHorseRaceName and ContestHorseRaceName2. It runs on a character.

label: Contest progress label
summary: The label above the progress-to-victory bar of a contest, saying what the viewer is doing in it.
details: It has 14 entries, for example "You are not competing", "You are Jousting" and "You are playing Board Games", with variants for recital, archery, horse race, duel and for being qualified or not. The active_competing entry appears twice in the list. It runs on a character.

label: Archery aptitude
summary: A colored rating word for how good the character is at archery contests: non-existent, terrible, poor, average, good or excellent.
details: Each rating from terrible up comes with an aptitude icon of its own level (1 for terrible, 2 for poor, 3 for average in the documented texts). It runs on a character.

label: On-foot aptitude
summary: A colored rating word for how good the character is at on-foot contests: non-existent, terrible, poor, average, good or excellent.
details: Same ratings and icons as the other aptitude texts. It runs on a character.

label: Horse aptitude
summary: A colored rating word for how good the character is at horse contests: non-existent, terrible, poor, average, good or excellent.
details: Same ratings and icons as the other aptitude texts. It runs on a character.

label: Wit aptitude
summary: A colored rating word for how good the character is at wit contests: non-existent, terrible, poor, average, good or excellent.
details: Same ratings and icons as the other aptitude texts. It runs on a character.

label: Contract or issue
summary: The name of a kind of task: Governance Issue, Settlement Issue, Ritual or Contract.
details: It runs on a character. The game's documentation does not say what decides which one is used.

label: Contract or issue concept
summary: The same four task kinds (governance issue, settlement issue, mandala ritual, task contract) as game concept links with a tooltip.
details: The plain-name version is GetContractOrIssue. It runs on a character.

label: Coronation site
summary: The name of the place where a coronation happens, such as the Palatine Chapel, the Hagia Sophia, Westminster Abbey or a local holding.
details: There are seven entries: Palatine Chapel, Hagia Sophia as cathedral, Hagia Sophia as mosque, Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Wawel Cathedral, Westminster Abbey and the local holding. The text of the last three is not documented; they are named by their keys. It runs on a province.

label: Coronation site prefix
summary: The word "the " (with a trailing space) in front of a coronation site name, or nothing.
details: The second entry is an empty text. It runs on a province.

label: Correct agent type, choice A
summary: The name of an agent type, such as Assassin, Lookout, Infiltrator or Footpad.
details: The game's documentation lists 41 agent types. Choice B has the identical list. It runs on a scheme. The game's documentation does not say how A and B differ in use.

label: Correct agent type, choice B
summary: The name of an agent type, such as Assassin, Lookout, Infiltrator or Footpad.
details: The game's documentation lists 41 agent types, the same as choice A. It runs on a scheme. The game's documentation does not say how A and B differ in use.

label: Council concept
summary: The game concept link "kurultai" or "council".
details: The link gives a tooltip when hovered. It runs on a character.

label: Council name, no tooltip
summary: The plain word "Kurultai" or "Council".
details: Same as the concept version but plain text without a tooltip. It runs on a character.

label: Council or court position
summary: The name of the position a character holds: the council title, the knight word, or all court and council positions they hold.
details: The first entry prints the character's council title. The second prints a lowercase word for a knight, taken from the game's text knight_culture_player_no_tooltip_lowercase (its name suggests it depends on culture). The third prints a string of every court and council position the character holds. It runs on a character.

label: Council or title name
summary: The character's council title, or the name of their landed title.
details: It runs on a character.

label: Council or title name, possessive
summary: The possessive of the character's council title, or of their landed title name.
details: It runs on a character.

label: Council position
summary: The name of a council position: Chancellor, Marshal, Steward, Spymaster or Court Chaplain.
details: The texts of the first four entries are documented; Court Chaplain is named by its key. It runs on a character.

label: Council window title
summary: The title word of the council window: kurultai, curia or council.
details: Kurultai and curia are the special names, council is the generic one. It runs on a character.

label: Councillor concept
summary: The game concept link "kurultai member" or "councillor".
details: The link gives a tooltip when hovered. It runs on a character.

label: Disaster recovery helper
summary: A name for who is available for disaster recovery: the kurultai, an entourage member, the minister of works or the steward.
details: The kurultai, minister of works and steward are concept links; the entourage one is a concept link followed by the word "member". The steward one is built from the name of the character's own steward position. It runs on a character.

label: Councillor or kurultai member
summary: The plain word "Kurultai Member" or "Councillor".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Councillor or kurultai member, possessive
summary: The possessive "Kurultai Member's" or "Councillor's".
details: The second entry key is spelled councillor_possive in the game's documentation, which looks like a typo in the game's own key. It runs on a character.

label: Court or camp
summary: The word "camp" or the word "court".
details: It runs on a character. The game's documentation does not say what decides which word is used.

label: Court concept
summary: The game concept link "camp" or "court".
details: The link gives a tooltip when hovered. It runs on a character.

label: Officer or court positions concept
summary: The concept link "officer positions" or "court positions".
details: Only the word "officer" and the whole "court positions" are links. It runs on a character.

label: Court owner word
summary: The word for whoever owns the court: "leader" or "liege".
details: The adventurer entry gives "leader", the liege entry gives "liege". It runs on a character.

label: Court owner concept
summary: A concept text for the court owner: the adventurer's type with its government icon, or the liege concept link.
details: The adventurer entry shows the government icon (if the character has a valid government) followed by the text from the custom text GetAdventurerType. It runs on a character.

label: Officer or court position
summary: The plain word "Officer" or "Court Position".
details: Capitalized plain text. It runs on a character.

label: Officers or court positions concept
summary: The concept link "officers" or "court positions".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Officers or court positions, plural
summary: The plain plural word "Officers" or "Court Positions".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Court position subject
summary: A subject a court position is about, such as swords, honor, patrols, raiding, daggers or flowers.
details: The game's documentation lists 34 subjects. The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry, so a text can name a random subject. It runs on a character.

label: Camp or court type
summary: The plain word "Camp" or "Court".
details: Capitalized, without a tooltip. It runs on a character.

label: Camp or court concept
summary: The game concept link "camp" or "court".
details: Same two entries as GetCourtConcept. It runs on a character.

label: Camps or courts, plural
summary: The plain plural word "Camps" or "Courts".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Follower or courtier
summary: The word "follower" or the word "courtier".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Follower or courtier concept
summary: The game concept link "follower" or "courtier".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Follower or courtier, by gender
summary: The word "follower" or "courtier", with separate entries for female and male.
details: The female and male entries print the same word in the documented texts. It runs on a character.

label: Courtier trait
summary: A word for a quality of a courtier: gluttony, curious ways, beauty, intellect and similar.
details: The game's documentation lists ten entries and the insanity entry appears twice. Insanity prints "curious ways". The rest are named for martial, diplomacy, stewardship, intrigue and prowess. It runs on a character.

label: Follower or courtier type
summary: The plain word "Follower" or "Courtier".
details: Capitalized, without a tooltip. It runs on a character.

label: Follower or courtier type concept
summary: The game concept link "follower" or "courtier".
details: Same two entries as GetCourtierConcept. It runs on a character.

label: Followers or courtiers, plural
summary: The plain plural word "Followers" or "Courtiers".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Followers or courtiers concept, plural
summary: The plural game concept link "followers" or "courtiers".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Camp or courtyard
summary: The word "camp" or the word "courtyard".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Cowed vassal protection note
summary: A note saying a vassal's protection lasts until a date, or nothing when the protection has no end date saved.
details: The first entry reads the remaining time of the variable temp_tributary_protection on the character and prints "(until date)" in a weak style. The second entry has no text at all. It runs on a character.

label: Crime
summary: The word for a character's crime, such as murderer, kinslayer, adulterer or heretic.
details: The game's documentation lists 15 entries: murderer, kinslayer, deviant, cannibal, sodomite, incestuous, adulterer, witch, fornicator, denounced, excommunicated, heretic, heathen, infidel and a fallback. It runs on a character.

label: Crime description
summary: A harsh descriptive phrase for a crime, such as "heartless butcherer" for murder or "familial traitor" for kinslaying.
details: It has one entry per crime in GetCrime, with a fallback. It runs on a character.

label: Crooked houses or tents
summary: The phrase "dilapidated tents" or "crooked houses".
details: Vanilla uses it in event texts that describe a poor part of a settlement. The game's documentation does not say what decides tents or houses. The entry key is spelled is_delapitated_tents, a typo in the game's own key. It runs on a character.

label: Marriage word
summary: A word for marriage: holy matrimony, blessed union, sacred bond, royal marriage, wedded union and similar.
details: The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry. It has 12 entries. It runs on a character.

label: Custodian synonym
summary: A word meaning custodian: custodian, guardian, protector, keeper or defender.
details: The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry, so a text can use a different synonym each time. It runs on a character.

label: Diarch appointment warning
summary: A tooltip warning that appointing a diarch will anger the liege's courtly vassals and cost opinion.
details: Entries cover an unrelated lowborn, a related lowborn, and a low, medium or high succession score, plus an empty one. Each says how many courtly vassals are offended and how much opinion they lose of the liege. The wording switches between "your"/"you" when the liege is the local player and "his"/"her"/"him"/"her" otherwise. The character is the one named in the text and the liege is that character's liege. It runs on a character.

label: Weak diarch succession score
summary: A tooltip saying that any character with a higher succession score than the diarch loses opinion of the liege, scaling with the difference.
details: It has a single entry. It runs on a character.

label: Daughter or son
summary: The word "daughter" or the word "son".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Daughter or son, possessive
summary: The possessive "daughter's" or "son's".
details: It runs on a character.

label: Derogatory word for a nonbeliever
summary: An insulting word for someone of another faith: heathen, infidel, barbarian or outsider.
details: The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry. It runs on a character.

label: Derogatory nonbelievers, plural
summary: The plural insulting word for people of another faith: infidels, heathens, outsiders or barbarians.
details: Unlike the singular version, the game does not mark this one for random picking. It runs on a character.

label: Descendant synonym
summary: A word meaning descendant: descendant, offspring, heir, progeny or scion.
details: The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry. It runs on a character.

label: Maneuver descriptor
summary: A word that describes a maneuver, such as Reverse, Double, Downward or Flying.
details: The game's documentation lists ten descriptors; the others are named abridged, lucky, royal, imperial, drunk and holy. The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry. It runs on a character.

label: Article a or an
summary: The article "a" or "an".
details: Vanilla puts it in front of a diarchy type name ("sharing power in a ..."). The game's documentation does not say how the choice is made. It runs on a character.

label: Diplomacy building
summary: The text "Large City", from an entry named after the building city_02.
details: It has just one entry. The game marks it as usable for picking a random entry, though with one entry the result is always the same. It runs on a character.

label: Disability
summary: The name of a physical or mental disability trait, such as Dwarf, Giant, Hunchbacked or Club-footed.
details: The game's documentation lists 28 entries: trait names from dwarf to dull, plus a fallback. It runs on a character.
